Scenario: The QA environment starts and is isolated
Preconditions: Throwaway QA environment started (section 1).
Steps:
1. Open http://localhost:3334/api/health.
2. Open http://localhost:4201.
Expected Result: Health returns {"status":"ok"}. The web app loads with the header "Pet Adoption". The pet list is empty, or shows only the demo pets if you seeded.

Scenario: A visitor browses the pet list and opens a pet
Preconditions: Signed out. At least 2 pets exist.
Steps:
1. Open /pets.
2. Click "View details" on a pet.
3. Click "Back to pets".
Expected Result: Cards show name, species, age, status and photo or "No image available". The detail page shows the description and status badge. Edit and Delete are not shown. The adoption section says "Interested in adopting <name>? Sign in to apply".

Scenario: Search, filter and sort the pet list
Preconditions: Pets with similar names and different species/status exist (e.g. demo data: Max, Maxi, Bella, Bello).
Steps:
1. Type part of a name in "Search pets by name..." and wait a moment.
2. Choose a species in "Filter by species".
3. Choose a status in "Filter by status".
4. Change "Sort by" to each option.
Expected Result: Results update after you stop typing and match case-insensitively anywhere in the name. "<n> pets found" matches the cards. Filters combine with the search. Sort order follows the chosen option. The URL contains the search, filters and sort.

Scenario: Pet list pagination keeps its state in the URL
Preconditions: More than 12 pets exist (demo data has 14).
Steps:
1. On /pets click "Next".
2. Open a pet on page 2, then use the browser Back button.
3. Refresh the page.
4. Change a filter.
Expected Result: "Page 2 of 2" is shown and the URL has page=2. Back and refresh return to the same page with the same filters. Changing a filter goes back to page 1. "Previous" is disabled on page 1 and "Next" on the last page.

Scenario: Register a new account
Preconditions: Signed out. An email address not registered yet.
Steps:
1. Click "Register".
2. Fill Name, Email and a password of at least 8 characters.
3. Click "Create account".
Expected Result: You land on /pets, signed in. The header shows your name, "Applications" and "Sign out". A welcome toast appears.

Scenario: Registration form validation
Preconditions: Signed out, on /register.
Steps:
1. Click "Create account" with all fields empty.
2. Enter an invalid email and a 5-character password, submit again.
Expected Result: Empty form: "Name is required.", "Email is required." and "Password must be at least 8 characters." Second attempt: "Enter a valid email address." and the password message. No request is sent and no account is created.

Scenario: Register with an email that already exists
Preconditions: An existing account (e.g. Owner).
Steps: 1. Signed out, register again with the same email in different letter case (e.g. OWNER@...).
Expected Result: Inline error "An account with this email already exists." You stay signed out on /register.

Scenario: Sign in with valid credentials
Preconditions: An existing account. Signed out.
Steps:
1. Click "Sign in".
2. Enter email and password.
3. Click "Sign in".
Expected Result: You land on /pets, signed in. Toast "Welcome back, <name>!".

Scenario: Sign in with a wrong password
Preconditions: An existing account. Signed out.
Steps: 1. Sign in with the right email and a wrong password.
Expected Result: Inline error "Incorrect email or password." You stay on /login, signed out.

Scenario: The session survives a refresh and a new tab
Preconditions: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Refresh the page.
2. Open http://localhost:4201/applications in a new tab of the same browser window.
Expected Result: You are still signed in in both tabs. The Applications page loads without asking you to sign in.

Scenario: Sign out
Preconditions: Signed in, on /applications.
Steps:
1. Click "Sign out".
2. Open /applications again (or use the browser Back button).
Expected Result: Toast "You have been signed out." The header shows "Sign in" and "Register". /applications redirects to /login.

Scenario: Protected pages redirect to sign-in and return afterwards
Preconditions: Signed out.
Steps:
1. Open /pets/new.
2. Sign in on the page you are sent to.
Expected Result: You are redirected to /login. After signing in you are back on /pets/new ("Add a pet"). The same works for /applications.

Scenario: Signing out in one tab affects the other tab
Preconditions: Signed in, two tabs open on a pet you could apply for.
Steps:
1. Sign out in tab 1.
2. In tab 2 (still showing the signed-in view) submit an application or save a form.
Expected Result: Nothing is saved. Tab 2 switches to the signed-out state: the pet page shows "Sign in to apply" (an error "Please sign in to continue." may show briefly); a form page redirects to /login.

Scenario: Repeated failed sign-ins are rate-limited
Preconditions: An existing account. Run this last: it blocks that account from this IP for 15 minutes.
Steps: 1. Sign in with a wrong password 6 times for the same email.
Expected Result:
Attempts 1-5 show "Incorrect email or password."; the 6th shows "Too many attempts. Please wait a few minutes and try again."
Cleanup: Wait 15 minutes, or restart the QA API (this also deletes all QA data).

Scenario: Signed-in users are sent away from sign-in and register pages
Preconditions: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Open /login.
2. Open /register.
Expected Result: Both pages immediately redirect you (to /pets) instead of showing the forms.

Scenario: Create a pet
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner.
Steps:
1. Click "Add a pet".
2. Fill Name, Species, Age (whole number) and Description.
3. Click "Create pet".
Expected Result: Toast "Pet created successfully." You land on the new pet's page with status "Available" and the Edit and Delete controls. The pet appears at the top of /pets (newest first).

Scenario: Pet form validation
Preconditions: Signed in, on "Add a pet".
Steps:
1. Click "Create pet" with empty fields.
2. Enter age "-1" or "2.5" and submit.
Expected Result: Messages "Name is required.", "Age is required." / "Age must be a non-negative whole number." and "Description is required." appear. Nothing is saved.

Scenario: Edit a pet
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner, on one of your pets.
Steps:
1. Click "Edit pet".
2. Change name, age and description.
3. Click "Save changes".
Expected Result: Toast "Pet updated successfully." The detail page and the list show the new values. The status is unchanged.

Scenario: Delete a pet after confirming
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner, a pet with no pending or accepted applications.
Steps:
1. On the pet page click "Delete".
2. Click "Cancel".
3. Click "Delete" again, then "Yes, delete".
Expected Result: Cancel keeps the pet. After confirming, toast "<name> was deleted.", you are taken to the list and the pet is gone.

Scenario: Other users cannot edit or delete a pet
Preconditions: Signed in as Adopter. A pet owned by Owner.
Steps:
1. Open the Owner's pet.
2. Open /pets/<that pet id>/edit directly.
Expected Result: No Edit or Delete controls on the pet page. The edit URL shows "You can only edit pets you posted." without a form.

Scenario: A pet with an active application cannot be deleted
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner, a pet with a pending (or accepted) application.
Steps: 1. On the pet page click "Delete", then "Yes, delete".
Expected Result: Error toast "This pet has open or accepted adoption applications and cannot be deleted." The pet stays.

Scenario: Edit page for a missing pet or failed load
Preconditions: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Open /pets/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/edit (valid-looking id that does not exist).
2. Open your own pet's edit page with the browser offline (DevTools > Network > Offline), then go online and click "Try again".
Expected Result: Missing pet: "Pet not found" and "Back to pets", no "Try again". Offline: "The server could not be reached. Check your connection and try again." with "Try again", which loads the form once online.

Scenario: Add a photo when creating a pet
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner. A JPEG or PNG under 5 MB without personal metadata.
Steps:
1. On "Add a pet" fill the fields and choose the photo in "Photo (optional)".
2. Click "Create pet".
Expected Result: A preview appears before saving. After saving, the photo shows on the pet page and on the card in the list. Opening the image in a new tab works (URL under http://localhost:3334/uploads/pets/).

Scenario: Replace and remove a photo
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner, a pet with a photo.
Steps:
1. Edit the pet, choose a different photo, save.
2. Edit again, click "Remove photo", save.
Expected Result: After replacing, the new photo is shown everywhere. After removing, the pet shows "No image available". Each save shows "Pet updated successfully."

Scenario: Wrong file type or too large a file is refused before upload
Preconditions: Signed in, on the pet form. A GIF (or PDF) and an image larger than 5 MB.
Steps:
1. Choose the GIF/PDF (switch the file dialog to "All files"; it offers only JPEG, PNG and WebP).
2. Choose the large image.
Expected Result: "Choose a JPEG, PNG or WebP image." and "The photo must be at most 5 MB." respectively. No preview; the file is not sent.

Scenario: A non-image renamed to .png is rejected by the server
Preconditions: Signed in, on "Add a pet". A text file renamed to fake.png.
Steps: 1. Fill the form, choose fake.png, click "Create pet".
Expected Result: The pet is created, then the toast says "The pet was saved, but the photo was not: Only JPEG, PNG and WebP photos are supported." The pet has no photo. (Assumes the browser reports the type from the extension, so the client check passes; unverified.)

Scenario: Apply to adopt another user's pet
Preconditions: Signed in as Adopter. An available pet owned by Owner.
Steps:
1. Open the pet.
2. Write a message in "Why would you like to adopt <name>?".
3. Click "Send application".
Expected Result: Toast "Your application was sent." The section shows "Your application:" "Pending" and "Withdraw". The pet status becomes "Pending". The application is listed under "My applications".

Scenario: Application message validation
Preconditions: Signed in as Adopter, on an available pet.
Steps:
1. Click "Send application" with an empty message.
2. Paste a message longer than 2000 characters and send.
Expected Result: "Please write a short message." and "The message must be at most 2000 characters." No application is created.

Scenario: Owners cannot apply for their own pet
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner.
Steps: 1. Open one of your own pets.
Expected Result: No application form. A "Review applications" button links to /applications instead.

Scenario: Withdraw a pending application and apply again
Preconditions: Signed in as Adopter with a pending application that is the only one for that pet.
Steps:
1. On /applications under "My applications" click "Withdraw".
2. Open the pet.
Expected Result: Toast "Application withdrawn." Status "Withdrawn" with no buttons. The pet is "Available" again and shows the application form, so you can apply again.

Scenario: A duplicate application is refused
Preconditions: Signed in as Adopter. The same available pet open in two tabs.
Steps:
1. Send an application in tab 1.
2. In tab 2 (still showing the form) send another one.
Expected Result: Tab 2 shows "You have already applied for this pet." inline. Only one application exists.

Scenario: Adopted pets cannot be applied for
Preconditions: Signed in as Adopter 2. A pet that is "Adopted" (not applied for by you).
Steps: 1. Open the adopted pet.
Expected Result: Status badge "Adopted" and no application form.

Scenario: The owner sees received applications with contact details
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner. Adopter has applied for one of your pets.
Steps: 1. Click "Applications" in the header.
Expected Result: Under "Applications for my pets" the application shows the pet name (link), "Submitted <date>", "Applicant: <name> (<email>)", the message, "Pending", and "Accept" and "Reject".

Scenario: Accepting adopts the pet and rejects the other applications
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner. Two pending applications for the same pet (Adopter and Adopter 2).
Steps:
1. Click "Accept" on Adopter's application.
2. Look at Adopter 2's application and at the pet.
Expected Result: Toast "Application accepted. The pet is now adopted." Adopter's application is "Accepted", Adopter 2's is "Rejected", neither has buttons. The pet is "Adopted". Adopter 2 sees "Rejected" under "My applications".

Scenario: Rejecting the last pending application makes the pet available
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner. A pet with exactly one pending application.
Steps:
1. Click "Reject" on it.
2. Open the pet.
Expected Result: Toast "Application rejected." Status "Rejected", no buttons. The pet is "Available". The rejected applicant sees "Rejected" and no new form for that pet.

Scenario: Application lists are paginated independently
Preconditions: Owner with more than 10 received applications (demo data: Ana has 11).
Steps:
1. Open /applications.
2. Click "Next" in "Applications for my pets".
3. Refresh, then use Back.
Expected Result: Page 2 shows the 11th application and "Page 2 of 2". The URL has receivedPage=2. "My applications" stays on its own page 1. Refresh keeps the page.

Scenario: Applications are private
Preconditions: Adopter applied for an Owner pet. Signed in as Adopter 2 (not involved).
Steps: 1. Open /applications.
Expected Result: Neither list shows that application or the Adopter's email.

Scenario: A stale decision in a second tab is refused
Preconditions: Signed in as Owner. Two pending applications for one pet; /applications open in two tabs.
Steps:
1. Tab 1: accept application 1.
2. Tab 2 (not refreshed): click "Reject" on application 1, then "Accept" on application 2.
Expected Result: Reject shows the error toast "This application has already been decided or withdrawn." Accept shows "This pet is no longer available for adoption." Nothing changes; refresh tab 2 to see application 1 "Accepted" and application 2 "Rejected".

Scenario: Empty application lists and a page past the end
Preconditions: Signed in as a user with no applications.
Steps:
1. Open /applications.
2. Open /applications?receivedPage=9 as a user with some received applications.
Expected Result: "No one has applied for your pets yet." and "You haven't applied to adopt any pets yet." Past the end: "There are no applications on this page." with "Go to the first page".

Scenario: Switch the language; it is remembered
Preconditions: Any page.
Steps:
1. Choose "Srpski" in the language selector in the header.
2. Navigate to another page, then refresh.
3. Switch back to "English".
Expected Result: The interface switches immediately (title "Udomljavanje ljubimaca", buttons and labels in Serbian) and stays Serbian after navigation and refresh. Pet names and descriptions are not translated (user content).

Scenario: Validation messages already on screen switch language
Preconditions: On /login, signed out.
Steps:
1. Click "Sign in" with empty fields.
2. Switch to "Srpski".
Expected Result: "Email is required." changes to "Email je obavezan." without resubmitting.

Scenario: The API is unreachable
Preconditions: On /pets. Use DevTools > Network > Offline (stopping the QA API would delete its data).
Steps:
1. Go offline and change a filter.
2. Go online and change the filter again.
Expected Result: After a few seconds (network errors are retried) "The server could not be reached. Check your connection and try again." Once online the list loads normally.

Scenario: Unknown pages and pet list pages past the end
Preconditions: Any user.
Steps:
1. Open /does-not-exist.
2. Open /pets?page=99.
3. Open /pets?page=abc.
Expected Result: "Page not found" with "Back to pets". page=99: "There are no pets on this page." with "Go to the first page". page=abc: page 1.

Scenario: No search results
Preconditions: On /pets.
Steps:
1. Search for "zzzz".
2. Click "Clear filters".
Expected Result: "No pets match your search." with "Clear filters"; clearing shows all pets again and empties the search box.

Scenario: The Docker stack runs the main journeys
Preconditions: Only when verifying the Docker setup. Back up first (README) - this uses persistent data.
Steps:
1. Start the Docker stack (section 1).
2. Check http://localhost:3333/api/health and http://localhost:4200.
3. Sign in, create a pet with a photo, apply as a second user, accept.
Expected Result:
All containers are "healthy". The journeys behave as in the QA environment; the photo URL is under http://localhost:3333/uploads/pets/ and still shows after `docker compose --profile app restart`.
Cleanup: Delete the test pet if it has no active application. Never use `down -v` on your normal environment.
